subject: Connectly renewal: proposed monthly commit bump & rate cap alignment
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@connectly.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@connectly.com
Date: 2026-08-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Connectly renewal: capacity planning and next steps

Hi Jordan,

Quick note from my side as we head into renewal: our product team has confirmed that July usage jumped roughly 2.8x versus May (see attached usage snapshot). We expect sustained higher traffic through Q4 as we roll out a new personalization feature.

High-level ask: can we increase our committed monthly tokens from 900k to 3.2M starting 2026-09-01, and align rate limits to support peak ingestion bursts (targeting ~250 requests/sec sustained for short windows)? We want to avoid throttling during user rollouts.

Questions for you:
- Is there a simple amendment path to increase commit and update rate caps on the Hosted API?
- What pricing / discount bands apply at that commit level?
- Can we get an estimated timeline for contract amendment + billing effective date?

I'm looping in procurement (procurement@connectly.com) — Emily Jones will own PO timelines. Attached: connectly-usage-report-2026-07.csv (summary).

Would love a short call this week to align. Thanks —

Daniel Park
Head of Platform Integrations
Connectly

Attachment: connectly-usage-report-2026-07.csv (CSV summary, 2 pages)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@connectly.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-07T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Connectly renewal: proposed monthly commit bump & rate cap alignment

Hi Daniel — thanks for the context and the usage file. Congrats on the rollout — that growth explains the ask.

Short answers: yes, we can do an amendment on Hosted API to raise committed tokens and to increase the per-customer rate cap windows. The commercial mechanics are straightforward but there are a couple of operational guardrails we'll want to confirm (burst pockets, soft-throttle fallback, invoice timing).

Initial proposal (ballpark, subject to contract language):
- Monthly committed tokens: move from 900,000 -> 3,200,000
- Unit price tier: pricing moves from Band B -> Band D (we'll apply volume discount at the higher commit)
- Rate limits: baseline 150 rps with a configurable burst pocket to cover 250 rps spikes for up to 15 minutes/day; we can discuss expanding burst windows if you expect longer sustained spikes.
- Effective date: we can target 2026-09-01 if we get a signed amendment by 2026-08-20 and a PO by 2026-08-27.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Ops draft an amendment and sizing note (cc Kimberly for the doc).
2) Procurement/Legal iterate on contract language.
3) We confirm invoicing cadence and any retroactive adjustments (if needed).

Kimberly/Karthik — can you put together a short amendment draft + sizing estimate and confirm whether the burst pocket described above is acceptable?

I'll set a 30-min sync with Daniel + Emily for next Tue/Wed — Daniel, what time zone works best?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Connectly amendment draft + sizing estimate attached

Thanks Jordan / Daniel — attaching a draft amendment and a sizing estimate to make the commercial terms concrete. Highlights below and notes on ops: 

Highlights (from draft):
- Commit: 3,200,000 tokens/month; 12-month renewal term (auto-renew opt-out)
- Pricing: tiered rate with 8% volume discount at this commit vs current list
- Burst pocket: +20% burst credit available per month (auto-applied as short bursts up to 15 minutes); sustained bursts longer than 15 minutes escalate to queued requests or optional temporary burst purchase.
- SLAs: standard Hosted API SLA applies; we include a one-time performance review window during the first 30 days of the new commit.

Ops notes:
- We can generally handle the request on Hosted API without Dedicated capacity. The burst pocket will be implemented via our throttling/burst policy; we will monitor KV cache behavior during the launch and may recommend small model variant pinning for latency-critical endpoints.
- If Connectly later needs fully sustained higher sustained rps (beyond burst windows), we should revisit Dedicated or a short-term reserved throughput add-on.

Attachments: 04-connectly-amendment-draft.docx, sizing-estimate.pdf

Action items for Connectly:
- Confirm the 3.2M commit and acceptance of the burst-window approach
- Provide PO template / billing instructions (Emily suggested she'll own this)
- Confirm any legal redlines (we'll track these in the amendment doc)

I'll also include a DocuSign draft link once Jordan confirms the language.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: 04-connectly-amendment-draft.docx (Word draft), sizing-estimate.pdf (2 pages)
